subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw add one canonical ignored descriptive string field to group/channel config entries, and if so should the field be `name`, `label`, or `description` and which channel entry schemas are in scope?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the public config contract and cross-channel scope are product decisions because OpenClaw avoids long-lived config aliases and requires schema/types/docs/metadata alignment.

options.title: Approve `name` across group entries
options.body: Use one optional `name: string` metadata field consistently across the relevant group/channel entry schemas and docs while leaving runtime behavior unchanged.

options.title: Choose a different canonical field
options.body: Pick `label` or `description` instead, but still implement only one canonical field across the same config contract surfaces.

options.title: Keep strict behavior-only entries
options.body: Decline metadata fields and leave users to document numeric group IDs outside `openclaw.json`.

recommendation.title: Approve `name` across group entries
recommendation.body: Use one optional `name: string` metadata field consistently across the relevant group/channel entry schemas and docs while leaving runtime behavior unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on config contracts, generated metadata/docs, and prior review of this exact issue.
